_note: Which application a script asset targets, how it is detected, and how it gets installed there. A script is the first asset type the library does not merely STORE - it has to end up somewhere an application will find it - and every application finds things differently. This file is that difference, as data.
_tags: An asset declares its targets as tags: app:houdini, app:maya, app:standalone. Tags and not the category, because the category is one folder and a tool can target two applications - a Python library used from both Houdini and Maya is one asset with two tags. The category stays the PRIMARY app, so the tree still reads.
_autodetect: `detect` patterns are a PRE-FILL, never a decision - the same rule as variant_patterns and guess_category. The Add window shows the detected tags as editable chips and the person keeps, adds or removes them. A pattern that looks right and is wrong is exactly the mistake someone catches at a glance and a rule never will.
_install: `install` names the mechanism, which is code in assetlib/install.py - one small writer per value, not a template engine. An app whose install is not implemented yet simply shows no button; the asset still imports, is searchable, and can be opened in Explorer. Adding an application is a row here plus one writer.

houdini.label: Houdini
houdini._install_note: A package JSON in $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/packages/ whose `path` points at the asset package. Houdini then contributes that package's toolbar/, python_panels/ and otls/ by itself. This is how THIS project installs itself (houdini/packages/assets_library.json) and how the eleven third-party packages already on this machine do it - FLOPs, Megascans, RenderMan, Octane. Install writes one file; uninstall deletes it; nothing of the user's is edited.
houdini._pref_dirs: Under the user's documents folder on Windows. Several versions are normally installed and an asset is installed into ONE of them, chosen at install time - a .py is version-agnostic but an .hda is not, and an H22 asset silently failing to load in H20.5 is worse than not offering it.

maya.label: Maya
maya._install_note: Not written yet. Maya has no package mechanism: it means a line in userSetup.py plus a shelf .mel in prefs/shelves, which EDITS files the user owns. That is a different promise from Houdini's and deserves its own decision rather than being assumed.

blender.label: Blender
blender._install_note: Not written yet. An addon is a zip Blender installs itself, or a folder dropped into scripts/addons.

nuke.label: Nuke
nuke._install_note: Not written yet. A line in ~/.nuke/menu.py, which is again a file the user owns.

standalone.label: Standalone
standalone._install_note: Deliberately none, and not a gap. A standalone tool is run from its own folder or a .bat; there is no host to install into, so the asset offers Open folder and nothing else. This is the fallback when no other app is detected.
